title: multi-env memory pathology: fragmented allocator + KV-index race causing transient GPU OOMs
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Multiple paying customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported intermittent GPU out-of-memory crashes and severe latency spikes during high-throughput chat workloads. Initial hotfixes mitigated immediate impact but further investigation revealed a combined failure mode: (1) allocator-level fragmentation that prevented large contiguous allocations and (2) a KV cache indexing race that temporarily inflated live reservation counts. Together these produced spikes in resident GPU memory and soft OOMs that manifested differently across environments (short-lived on Hosted, persistent on Private).

Scope & Symptoms:
- Affected environments: hosted-api clusters (us-west), several dedicated pools during burst traffic, 2 customer Private deployments (on-prem).
- Symptoms: unexpected token-generation failures, session restarts, elevated tail latency, and in some cases node reboots driven by driver-level OOM.
- Frequency: tied to mixed-length prompt patterns and bursts of prefix cache population.
- First reported: 2025-02-11 14:03 UTC (customer escalation).

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Emergency rate caps on affected routes for hosted customers to reduce prefix growth (applied 2025-02-11 16:20 UTC).
- Temporary eviction override: force-evict oldest KV prefixes above a conservative memory threshold (deployed hot on dedicated pools 2025-02-12 01:10 UTC).
- Customer-facing communication sent to impacted customers with recommended short-term prompts/size limits.

Diagnosis summary:
Root cause is multi-factorial: the runtime allocator uses segregated free lists and a best-fit variant that, under mixed allocation size churn, produced many small free extents that could not be coalesced quickly. Long-lived pinned tensors (from large KV prefix caches) prevented movement/compaction. Concurrently, a race in the KV cache's index update path allowed two threads to temporarily overcount live entries during concurrent evict/insert cycles, which caused the memory accounting to under-report pressure and delayed eviction activation. The combination allowed resident memory to grow beyond practical coalescing thresholds and caused driver-level failed allocations for large attention/FFN buffers.

Fixes implemented in runtime-1.19-patch1:
- Allocator: added on-free coalescing and a background defragmenter that opportunistically merges adjacent free extents when the fragmentation metric (gpu_free_frag_pct) exceeds 18%. This is conservative to avoid extra GPU work.
- KV cache: fixed a race in index update by strengthening the ordering on index bitmap updates and adding a small per-shard compare-and-swap guard. This eliminates the transient overcount condition.
- Cache policy: introduced probabilistic prefix cap with LRU+size-awareness to limit runaway prefix growth in bursty workloads.
- Guards: added a safe-fail path that falls back to a smaller kv-compact pass when very large contiguous allocations fail, instead of immediately OOMing.

Testing & Verification:
- Unit + stress tests added for the allocator coalescing edge cases and for high-concurrency kv index churn.
- Resimulated customer traffic (using recorded workloads) on a canary dedicated pool with synthetic fragmentation injection; no OOMs observed across 72-hour run.
- Private customer test: staged upgrade with on-site support and pre-upgrade snapshot + rollback validated.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary rollout to low-traffic hosted clusters (canary-1) — started 2025-02-18.
2) Expand to dedicated pools with controlled concurrency and monitor fragmentation metrics — targeted 2025-02-20.
3) Coordinate Private customer upgrades with SRE + Solutions — windows scheduled 2025-02-21 to 2025-02-24.

Monitoring & Alerts added:
- Metrics: gpu_free_frag_pct, kv_index_inflight_ops, prefix_count_per_session, session_alloc_pattern_histogram.
- Alerts: gpu_free_frag_pct > 25% for 5m triggers P0 pager; kv_index_inflight_ops > 50 sustained for 3m triggers on-call.
- Dashboards: runtime-allocator health, kv-cache hot-shard view, per-customer memory growth tail charts.

Customer comms & follow up:
- Customer support threads: contained, with patch timeline and remediation steps. Two customers required private deployments to be rolled back once before stable upgrade window confirmed.
- Follow-ups: improve canary automation for fragmentation injection, long-term allocator redesign spike (RFC), and a playbook for rapid private upgrade coordination.

Outcomes so far:
- Hotfix merged (PR 4123) and cherry-picked to stable branch. Canary shows stable memory patterns. No new OOM escalations in 48h post-rollout on canary.

Open actions:
- ENG-18378 (allocator telemetry improvement): add per-allocation-size histograms.
- ENG-18379 (kv-cache eviction tuning): iterate on probabilistic cap parameters using customer workloads.
- Postmortem writeup and exec summary to be finalized (link in attachments).
